templates.name: Dock Union Standoff
templates.summary: Union pickets block a bonded cargo while the Watch threatens dispersal.

cues.signal: The union steward demands wage escrow before the Watch bell’s sixth toll.
cues.inference: The demand, deadline, and fallback are explicit.

cues.signal: Watch Intervention 2/6; at full, the square is cleared by force.
cues.inference: The confrontation has a bounded danger clock.

stakes.headline: Secure passage without sacrificing workers or let the Watch define the outcome.

approaches.label: Spend the payroll ledger to prove withheld wages

onSuccess.summary: The employer funds escrow and the union releases the cargo.

onPartial.summary: Cargo moves, but the Council blames the player for the public settlement.

onFailure.summary: The ledger is challenged and the Watch closes in.

approaches.lockout: payroll-ledger is consumed on success or discredited on refusal; its topic cannot be replayed.

approaches.label: Call Sister Merrow as neutral arbiter

onSuccess.summary: A bonded settlement releases cargo and defers final wages.

onFailure.summary: The Council rejects the arbiter and spends her credibility.

approaches.lockout: Merrow’s credibility can be spent once in this confrontation.

approaches.label: Walk away and concede the night shipment

onSuccess.summary: The standoff ends; the Watch seizes the shipment and the player preserves the ledger.

onFailure.summary: The route closes and is removed rather than offered again.

approaches.lockout: Walking away always ends the current confrontation and applies the declared concession/cooldown.

config.onRepeat: consume/discredit leverage, advance danger, or lock approach

forcedTerminal.summary: The Watch disperses the square, seizes cargo, and arrests pickets; the confrontation ends.

resolution.antiRepeatRule: No unchanged leverage topic may be selected twice; withdrawal terminates and starts cooldown.

example.telegraphProse: The steward names wage escrow and the sixth bell while the intervention clock reveals the Watch’s exact fallback.
example.stakesProse: Spend the one-use payroll ledger, call a neutral arbiter whose credibility can be spent, or leave and concede the shipment.
example.resolutionProse: Every argument consumes leverage or advances a clock; at eight turns the Watch action commits and the scene cannot pad.
example.receiptProse: The receipt records cargo custody, union/Watch standing, NPC arrests or settlement, and the next quest.

templates.name: The Salt Clerk’s Betrayal
templates.summary: A trusted clerk sells the player’s route list to customs and asks for protection.

cues.signal: The route list bears fresh customs pinholes and the clerk’s ink is missing.
cues.inference: The betrayal is evidenced before confrontation.

cues.signal: The clerk asks for passage on the dawn packet in exchange for naming the buyer.
cues.inference: The confession has a concrete price and deadline.

stakes.headline: Extract the buyer’s name, turn the clerk over, or protect them and absorb the political cost.

approaches.label: Spend the matched ink proof to force a confession

onSuccess.summary: The clerk names the buyer and accepts protective custody.

onPartial.summary: The buyer is named, but the clerk escapes before custody.

onFailure.summary: The clerk contests the proof and customs nears.

approaches.lockout: ink-match is consumed on success or discredited on refusal; its topic cannot be replayed.

approaches.label: Grant passage on the dawn packet

onSuccess.summary: Protection buys the name and keeps the clerk alive.

onFailure.summary: The seat cannot be guaranteed, so the offer becomes invalid.

approaches.lockout: The packet seat is spent or invalidated once.

approaches.label: Walk away and let customs take the clerk

onSuccess.summary: The confrontation ends; the clerk enters customs custody and the buyer remains hidden.

onFailure.summary: The route closes and is removed rather than offered again.

approaches.lockout: Walking away always ends the current confrontation and applies the declared concession/cooldown.

config.onRepeat: consume/discredit leverage, advance danger, or lock approach

forcedTerminal.summary: Customs takes the clerk and the immediate confession opportunity closes.

resolution.antiRepeatRule: No unchanged leverage topic may be selected twice; withdrawal terminates and starts cooldown.

example.telegraphProse: Pinholes and missing ink prove the route list was copied, while the clerk names the dawn-packet price.
example.stakesProse: Spend the ink match, spend a unique packet seat, or leave the clerk to customs custody.
example.resolutionProse: Proof and passage cannot be reused; customs arrives by turn six and converts the unresolved crisis into a prison-barge hook.
example.receiptProse: The system records confession, buyer intel, custody, passage asset, faction standing, and the appropriate follow-up.

templates.name: Flood Levy Deadline
templates.summary: The council will condemn one ward unless the player assembles funding or proves fraud.

cues.signal: Levy Vote 3/6; at full, Low Cape is condemned.
cues.inference: The political deadline and consequence are visible.

cues.signal: Merchant Council will fund two segments in exchange for warehouse immunity.
cues.inference: A costly acceleration path is explicit.

stakes.headline: Save Low Cape without granting permanent immunity, or choose which cost the district carries.

approaches.label: Spend the verified drainage audit to expose fraud

onSuccess.summary: The fraud finding voids the condemnation vote.

onPartial.summary: The ward is saved, but the Council excludes the player from committee access.

onFailure.summary: The audit is challenged and the vote accelerates.

approaches.lockout: verified-drainage-audit is consumed on success or discredited on refusal; its topic cannot be replayed.

approaches.label: Trade warehouse immunity for emergency funding

onSuccess.summary: Funding saves the ward while merchants gain declared immunity.

onFailure.summary: The merchants withdraw the offer and it cannot be repeated.

approaches.lockout: The immunity offer is accepted or withdrawn once.

approaches.label: Walk away and evacuate Low Cape

onSuccess.summary: The vote proceeds; the player pivots to evacuation rather than repeating debate.

onFailure.summary: The route closes and is removed rather than offered again.

approaches.lockout: Walking away always ends the current confrontation and applies the declared concession/cooldown.

config.onRepeat: consume/discredit leverage, advance danger, or lock approach

forcedTerminal.summary: The vote condemns Low Cape and the crisis ends in an evacuation arc.

resolution.antiRepeatRule: No unchanged leverage topic may be selected twice; withdrawal terminates and starts cooldown.

example.telegraphProse: The vote clock states the condemnation result, and the merchants’ immunity price appears as a named political cost.
example.stakesProse: Spend the audit, trade immunity for funding, or abandon debate and begin evacuation.
example.resolutionProse: Every maneuver moves defense or vote clocks; turn eight condemns the ward and opens a different objective.
example.receiptProse: Receipts preserve ward status, residents, council/merchant standing, access, audit consumption, and evacuation or fraud quests.

templates.name: Night Market Seizure
templates.summary: The Watch moves to confiscate unlicensed stalls while two factions claim authority.

cues.signal: A posted order lists confiscation at moonrise and names the officer authorized to suspend it.
cues.inference: The operation, deadline, and decision-maker are known.

cues.signal: Stallkeepers chain carts into three defensible lanes.
cues.inference: Escalation geometry and a withdrawal route are visible.

stakes.headline: Keep the market open, evacuate it intact, or let confiscation redefine district control.

approaches.label: Spend the harbor jurisdiction writ

onSuccess.summary: The Watch suspends seizure under superior harbor authority.

onPartial.summary: The market stays open for one week under hostile probation.

onFailure.summary: The officer rejects the writ and begins confiscation.

approaches.lockout: harbor-jurisdiction-writ is consumed on success or discredited on refusal; its topic cannot be replayed.

approaches.label: Organize a three-lane stall evacuation

onSuccess.summary: The goods escape before the Watch can seize them.

onFailure.summary: One cache is seized and the lanes narrow.

approaches.lockout: Each failed lane closes; the evacuation topology changes.

approaches.label: Walk away and concede the market

onSuccess.summary: The Watch takes the market and the current confrontation ends.

onFailure.summary: The route closes and is removed rather than offered again.

approaches.lockout: Walking away always ends the current confrontation and applies the declared concession/cooldown.

config.onRepeat: consume/discredit leverage, advance danger, or lock approach

forcedTerminal.summary: Moonrise confiscation completes and the encounter becomes a recovery arc.

resolution.antiRepeatRule: No unchanged leverage topic may be selected twice; withdrawal terminates and starts cooldown.

example.telegraphProse: The seizure order names moonrise and Lieutenant Vale, while chained stalls reveal the three-lane evacuation plan.
example.stakesProse: Spend the writ, evacuate changing lanes, or concede control and end the standoff immediately.
example.resolutionProse: The writ is one-use and evacuation failures close lanes; the seventh turn commits confiscation and a recovery quest.
example.receiptProse: The ledger records market control, goods, Watch and stallkeeper standing, network access, and recovery or charter hooks.

templates.name: Reef Fever Allocation
templates.summary: A limited antitoxin shipment can protect dockworkers or reef refugees, not both.

cues.signal: The crate holds twelve sealed doses; both clinics require nine before dawn.
Both physicians state the mortality and political consequences of receiving only three doses.
cues.inference: Each branch has declared human and faction stakes.

stakes.headline: Allocate scarce medicine with no hidden option to save everyone.

approaches.label: Spend the cargo manifest to requisition three reserve doses

onSuccess.summary: Three reserve doses become available at the cost of one turn.

onPartial.summary: Two doses arrive while customs opens an inquiry.

onFailure.summary: The manifest fails and dawn approaches.

approaches.lockout: antitoxin-cargo-manifest is consumed on success or discredited on refusal; its topic cannot be replayed.

approaches.label: Split six doses to each clinic

onSuccess.summary: Both clinics receive partial protection and both suffer declared losses.

onFailure.summary: If custody is invalid, the split is blocked and the crate is quarantined.

approaches.lockout: The sealed crate can be allocated once; no dose duplication is possible.

approaches.label: Walk away and let the health board choose

onSuccess.summary: The board allocates by policy and the player loses control of the decision.

onFailure.summary: The route closes and is removed rather than offered again.

approaches.lockout: Walking away always ends the current confrontation and applies the declared concession/cooldown.

config.onRepeat: consume/discredit leverage, advance danger, or lock approach

forcedTerminal.summary: Dawn arrives without allocation; both clinics suffer and containment begins.

resolution.antiRepeatRule: No unchanged leverage topic may be selected twice; withdrawal terminates and starts cooldown.

example.telegraphProse: The visible dose count and physicians’ estimates establish that no hidden perfect allocation exists.
example.stakesProse: Use the one-use manifest to seek reserves, split the crate with known losses, or surrender the choice to the board.
example.resolutionProse: Inventory cannot duplicate; dawn advances with attempts and the fifth turn converts delay into containment.
example.receiptProse: The receipt stores exact clinic coverage, casualties, dose inventory, customs/board standing, favors, and recovery hooks.

templates.name: Black Ledger Exposure
templates.summary: A journalist will publish a ledger that implicates both enemies and allies unless the player shapes the release.

cues.signal: Editor Saye names the print deadline and the three redactions she will accept.
cues.inference: Publication and modification paths are bounded.

cues.signal: Press Run 2/6; at full, the unredacted ledger becomes public.
cues.inference: Exposure has an exact terminal event.

stakes.headline: Publish truth, protect vulnerable sources, or suppress the ledger at a lasting trust cost.

approaches.label: Spend the verified source chain to require safe redactions

onSuccess.summary: The ledger publishes with the agreed source protections.

onPartial.summary: Sources are protected, but reformers accuse the player of concealment.

onFailure.summary: The editor rejects interference and publication accelerates.

approaches.lockout: verified-source-chain is consumed on success or discredited on refusal; its topic cannot be replayed.

approaches.label: Trade an exclusive interview for named redactions

onSuccess.summary: The interview purchases limited, visible redactions.

onFailure.summary: The editor rejects the trade and it cannot be offered again.

approaches.lockout: The exclusive is one-use; rejection removes it.

approaches.label: Walk away and accept unredacted publication

onSuccess.summary: The confrontation ends and every named actor faces the declared fallout.

onFailure.summary: The route closes and is removed rather than offered again.

approaches.lockout: Walking away always ends the current confrontation and applies the declared concession/cooldown.

config.onRepeat: consume/discredit leverage, advance danger, or lock approach

forcedTerminal.summary: The presses complete and the exposure crisis ends with source-protection work.

resolution.antiRepeatRule: No unchanged leverage topic may be selected twice; withdrawal terminates and starts cooldown.

example.telegraphProse: Editor Saye names the print deadline and acceptable redactions while the press clock shows when publication becomes irreversible.
example.stakesProse: Spend the source chain, trade a one-use exclusive, or leave and accept unredacted fallout.
example.resolutionProse: Leverage is consumed or rejected; at seven turns publication commits and the debate cannot recur.
example.receiptProse: The outcome stores publication form, source safety, press/reform standing, editor relationship, intel, and follow-ups.

templates.name: Harbormaster Leverage Negotiation
templates.summary: The Harbormaster controls a quarantine berth and will trade access for silence or verified public cover.

cues.signal: A blue-wax permit links the Harbormaster’s clerk to an illegal berth sale.
cues.inference: The evidence has specific provenance and relevance.

cues.signal: The Harbormaster offers one berth in exchange for the permit before the tide turns.
cues.inference: The concession, cost, and deadline are explicit.

stakes.headline: Secure quarantine access without creating an infinitely reusable threat.

approaches.label: Spend the blue-wax permit to demand berth access

onSuccess.summary: The evidence compels one berth authorization.

onPartial.summary: Access opens for one voyage while the office turns hostile.

onFailure.summary: The permit is dismissed and the access window shrinks.

approaches.lockout: blue-wax-permit is consumed on success or discredited on refusal; its topic cannot be replayed.

approaches.label: Trade silence for a one-voyage berth

onSuccess.summary: A binding silence promise buys one voyage.

onFailure.summary: Prior conduct makes the trade unavailable.

approaches.lockout: The silence promise is bound once and later violations have authored consequences.

approaches.label: Walk away and miss the tide window

onSuccess.summary: The tide window closes and the player must pursue another route.

onFailure.summary: The route closes and is removed rather than offered again.

approaches.lockout: Walking away always ends the current confrontation and applies the declared concession/cooldown.

config.onRepeat: consume/discredit leverage, advance danger, or lock approach

forcedTerminal.summary: The tide turns, ending this negotiation and opening the reef anchorage route.

resolution.antiRepeatRule: No unchanged leverage topic may be selected twice; withdrawal terminates and starts cooldown.

example.telegraphProse: The blue-wax permit proves the berth sale and Oren names the exact silence-for-access trade before the tide turns.
example.stakesProse: Consume the permit, bind a one-voyage silence promise, or leave and lose this tide window.
example.resolutionProse: Every leverage item becomes consumed, bound, or discredited; turn five closes the berth and creates a new route.
example.receiptProse: The receipt stores berth scope, permit/promise state, Oren and Harbor Office reactions, and the follow-up route.

templates.name: Silk Lane Political Ambush
templates.summary: A knife crew stages an attack to make the player appear responsible for faction violence.

cues.signal: Shop shutters close in sequence and a dropped campaign ribbon points against the wind.
cues.inference: A coordinated frame-up ambush is about to begin.

cues.signal: A courier warns that three pamphleteers are waiting to report the first blade drawn.
cues.inference: Witness control is the true objective.

stakes.headline: Survive without validating the attackers’ public narrative.

approaches.label: Expose the planted campaign ribbon to the witnesses

onSuccess.summary: The witnesses recognize the frame-up and the crew withdraws.

onPartial.summary: The attack ends, but public opinion splits.

onFailure.summary: The evidence looks planted by the player and blame accelerates.

approaches.lockout: planted-campaign-ribbon is consumed on success or discredited on refusal; its topic cannot be replayed.

approaches.label: Turn the pamphleteers by protecting them from the first volley

onSuccess.summary: Protected witnesses identify the attackers and break the frame.

onFailure.summary: A witness is wounded and blame rises.

approaches.lockout: Each cover position can protect once; wounded witnesses change the next option.

approaches.label: Escape through the dye yard and accept suspicion

onSuccess.summary: The player escapes alive, but the attackers control the first public account.

onFailure.summary: The route closes and is removed rather than offered again.

approaches.lockout: Walking away always ends the current confrontation and applies the declared concession/cooldown.

config.onRepeat: consume/discredit leverage, advance danger, or lock approach

forcedTerminal.summary: The false account reaches print, the attackers escape, and the scene ends in a name-clearing arc.

resolution.antiRepeatRule: No unchanged leverage topic may be selected twice; withdrawal terminates and starts cooldown.

example.telegraphProse: Closing shutters, an impossible ribbon, and waiting pamphleteers reveal that the ambush targets reputation as much as life.
example.stakesProse: Spend the ribbon proof, protect witnesses through changing cover, or flee and accept suspicion.
example.resolutionProse: Witness and blame clocks advance; by turn six the account prints and the confrontation ends in a clear-your-name quest.
example.receiptProse: The system records witness states, attacker identity, public opinion, escape location, intel, and the next political beat.
